name: deploy-check
description: Answers "did my deploy actually work?" — catches pages that return 200 while rendering nothing, broken links, stray noindex, and staging that never updated.
long_description:
200 OK is not the same as "it works". A page can return 200, weigh 41 KB, and show a human absolutely nothing — that is what a JavaScript bundle that threw looks like from the outside, and what a deploy that published the wrong directory looks like too.

This extension gives Claude three read-only tools:

- **check_page** — status, redirect chain, response time, and the signal nobody checks: how much visible text the page actually renders. Plus title, meta description, viewport, canonical, og:image, and a stray noindex left over from staging.
- **check_links** — every link on a page, checked. HEAD first with a GET fallback, so servers that refuse HEAD are never mistaken for dead links. Capped and concurrency-limited so it stays polite.
- **compare_pages** — two URLs, same signals. Staging against production, or the same URL before and after a release. If both render identical text, the deploy has not landed.

It does not run JavaScript, on purpose: it reads the page the way a crawler, a link preview and a first paint see it. The honest consequence is that a healthy single-page app looks identical to a broken one in raw HTML, so blank HTML is only reported as a hard failure when the page loads no scripts at all. With scripts present you get a warning that says plainly that this tool cannot tell the two apart.

No account, no API key, no telemetry. Everything runs on your machine.

tools.name: check_page
tools.description: Check a URL is up and actually rendering: status, redirects, response time, visible text length, and the head tags that decide how it looks in a tab, a search result and a shared link.

tools.name: check_links
tools.description: Read every link on a page and check each one resolves, without mistaking a server that refuses HEAD for a dead link.

tools.name: compare_pages
tools.description: Compare two URLs and report where they differ, to answer whether a deploy actually landed.
